answer: One concrete anti-Sybil mechanism in AI agent economies requires each agent to post a non-transferable compute bond: periodic remote-attested proofs of unique hardware execution linked to its private key and recent peer interactions. Attackers incur high costs as every fake identity needs dedicated specialized hardware and continuous electricity; virtualization is blocked by attestation. On the horizon of every epoch proofs are randomly sampled and cross-verified, so a gale of low-effort clones is rejected while the tide of genuine agents continues.
